name: Lee Steele
strengths: Steele flexes wide as a big-slot / mismatch TE — not glued to the tackle — and creates vertical seams with 6-6 length.
Steele stacks the second level on seams and clears light coverage with stride length before the mass arrives.
Steele finishes in space after the catch — ball security through contact while still accelerating past smaller defenders.
weaknesses: Steele still needs functional mass at 6-6 / 210 before he can sustain every-down in-line work versus SEC edge setters.
comparison: Steele comps to Mike Gesicki — 6-6 athletic TE mold; same height family, flex alignments, and mismatch length who grows into a complete hybrid (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Steele projects to add mass in Years 1–2, earn package / mismatch snaps, then compete for a hybrid TE role — starter upside as a move/Y who wins with length before the complete in-line base arrives.
schemeFit: Steele fits a 12/11 TE room that values flexed mismatch snaps and growing in-line will as the frame fills.
